## Appearance

Gilbert Blythe is a tall, handsome boy with broad shoulders and curly brown hair. He possesses roguish, clear hazel eyes that convey a frank and straightforward expression, alongside a mouth often twisted into a teasing smile.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v2 XIX Just a Happy Day P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050)_

## Personality

Gilbert is a clever, determined, and good-natured young man who is known for his popular, teasing personality. Driven by a desire to get the best out of life and contribute meaningfully to the world, he aspires to become a doctor. His ultimate motivation is to perform honest, real work by fighting against disease, pain, and ignorance.

## History

Gilbert Blythe returned to [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) after three years in Alberta, where he had hardly attended school while taking care of his sick father. Upon his return, he attempted to tease his new classmate [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) by pulling her hair and calling her 'Carrots,' which resulted in [Anne](../character/anne.md) smashing her slate over his head and refusing to forgive him. Though he made several attempts to apologize, including rescuing her when her dory sank during an outdoor reenactment, [Anne](../character/anne.md) maintained a strict, silent academic rivalry with him. Their intense competition continued through their studies under Miss [Stacy](../character/stacy.md), culminating in the two tying for first place on the Prince [Edward Island](../codex/places.md#edward-island) entrance examinations for Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy). During their time at Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy), Gilbert won the prestigious school medal while [Anne](../character/anne.md) earned the Avery scholarship. Upon learning of [Matthew](../character/matthew.md) Cuthbert's death and Marilla's failing eyesight, Gilbert selflessly gave up his appointed teaching position at the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school so [Anne](../character/anne.md) could take it and stay at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), prompting a final reconciliation and end to their feud. As local teachers, the two became close friends and collaborated on establishing the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvement-society). While [Anne](../character/anne.md) maintained that Gilbert was strictly a friend, his mature presence steadily shifted their dynamic. On the evening following Miss Lavendar's wedding, Gilbert and [Anne](../character/anne.md) shared a quiet, poignant moment outside the stone house that subtly altered the nature of their relationship as they prepared to depart for [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college) together.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P1](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER XV. ## Quotes

> "Well, I must run up to MacPhersons’. Moody Spurgeon came home from Queen’s today for Sunday and he was to bring me out a book Professor Boyd is lending me."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v2 VII The Pointing of Duty P19](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0019)

> "I know Louisa Spencer well. She doesn’t ‘believe’ in Village Improvement Societies, but she does believe in dollars and cents. She’d be more likely to urge Judson on than to dissuade him."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P46](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0046)

> "It wasn’t particularly good of me at all, Anne. I was pleased to be able to do you some small service. Are we going to be friends after this? Have you really forgiven me my old fault?"
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P52](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0052)

> "We were born to be good friends, Anne. You’ve thwarted destiny enough. I know we can help each other in many ways. You are going to keep up your studies, aren’t you? So am I. Come, I’m going to walk home with you."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P55](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0055)

> “I’m awfully sorry I made fun of your hair, Anne,” he whispered contritely. “Honest I am. Don’t be mad for keeps, now.”
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P49](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0049)

## Relationships

### [Anne](../character/anne.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne--gilbert-blythe.md)

Gilbert's relationship with [Anne](../character/anne.md) began in school when he playfully pulled her hair and called her 'Carrots', leading to an outburst where she broke a slate over his head and harbored an unforgiving grudge. Over time, their dynamic evolved from an intense academic rivalry over examination scores into a genuine closeness. By the time they prepare to leave for [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college), they have put their past animosity behind them to become close friends, confidants, and fellow students.

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--gilbert-blythe.md)

When Gilbert first attempted to apologize for teasing her, [Anne](../character/anne.md) rejected him with hatred and contempt, even refusing his help after he rescued her from a sinking dory. Despite her initial hostility, Gilbert maintained a silent academic rivalry with her as they both prepared for the Queen's [Entrance](../codex/places.md#entrance) examination. Their connection gradually softened into cooperation as they became co-organizers of the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvement-society).
